name: Gilalai
overview: Gilalai was a male Levite known for his role involving musical instruments, as noted in Nehemiah 12:36. His identity as a Levite highlights his participation in the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Gilalai appears in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin provided. It is simply recognized as a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 12:36.
familyAndRelationships: Gilalai is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his tribal lineage within the priestly family. Scripture does not record any other family relationships beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Gilalai's significance lies in his association with the Levites who served in the temple, specifically through the use of musical instruments. This role underscores the importance of worship and praise in the life of Israel, with Levites like Gilalai contributing to the spiritual atmosphere during temple services. His mention in Nehemiah 12:36 places him within the context of the post-exilic restoration of worship in Jerusalem.
